explain.ja: 銀将は、斜め4方向に1マス動けるのに加えて、真正面のマスにも1マス動けます。
explain.en: The silver moves one square in each of the four diagonal directions, and also one square straight forward.

section.ja: 銀の動き方、斜め4方向1マス+正面
section.en: How the silver moves: one square in four diagonal directions plus straight ahead

explain.ja: 銀が成ると成銀になり、金将と同じ動きになります。縦横1マスと斜め前に動けるようになり、進める方向が大きく変わります。銀は攻めにも守りにも使えるバランスのよい駒です。開始時点で盤上に2枚あるので、1枚は玉の近くにくっつけて守りに、1枚は前に繰り出して攻めに使うのがセオリーです。初心者に多い矢倉戦法や四間飛車の駒組みを見ると、玉の近くに守りの銀、飛車の近くに攻めの銀がいます。
explain.en: A promoted silver moves like gold: one square orthogonally and diagonally forward, so its directions change greatly. Silver is a balanced piece usable for both attack and defence. Since there are two on the board at the start, the standard is to keep one near the king for defence and bring the other forward to attack. In the Yagura and Fourth File Rook setups popular with beginners, a defensive silver is near the king and an attacking silver near the rook.

section.ja: 成銀の動き方、成ると金の動きに
section.en: How the promoted silver moves: promoted, it moves like a gold

title.en: Piece development of the Yagura strategy

explain.ja: 銀は攻めにも守りにも使えるバランスの良い駒です。盤上には銀が2枚あるので、1枚は玉の近くで守りに、もう1枚は前に出して攻めに使うのがセオリーです。矢倉戦法と四間飛車の駒組みでは、玉の近くに守りの銀、飛車の近くに攻めの銀がいます。
explain.en: Silver is a well-balanced piece that can be used for both attack and defense. Since each side has two silvers, the standard approach is to keep one near the king for defense and advance the other for attack. In Yagura and Fourth-File Rook setups, the defending silver is near the king and the attacking silver is near the rook.

title.ja: 図1-1 銀をどちらに進める？
title.en: Figure 1-1: Which way to advance the silver?

explain.ja: 銀は斜め方向には自由に動けますが、縦横の動きは得意ではなく、横と後ろには動けません。斜めの動きを最大限に利用して、ジグザグに(千鳥に)使うのがよいです。たとえば図1-1から銀を縦に動かした場合とジグザグに動かした場合を考えます。
explain.en: The silver moves freely diagonally but is poor at orthogonal moves; it cannot move sideways or backward. It is best to exploit its diagonal movement by using it in a zigzag (chidori) fashion. Consider moving the silver straight versus zigzag from Figure 1-1.

section.ja: 銀は千鳥に使え!!斜めに動かして使おう
section.en: Use the silver in a zigzag! Move it diagonally

title.ja: 図1-2 前に進めると歩で取られてしまう
title.en: Figure 1-2: If advanced forward, it gets captured by a pawn

explain.ja: ▲5六銀と銀をまっすぐ進めると、△5五歩と打たれて銀を取られる形になります。銀はまっすぐ進めると元の位置に戻れないので、取られてしまうことがあります。前に進めるときは慎重にしましょう。
explain.en: If the silver is advanced straight with ▲5六銀, White's △5五歩 drop leaves it capturable. A silver advanced straight cannot return to its original square, so it can be lost. Be careful when advancing it.

section.ja: 銀は千鳥に使え!!斜めに動かして使おう
section.en: Use the silver in a zigzag! Move it diagonally

title.ja: 図1-3 銀は千鳥に使え
title.en: Figure 1-3: Use the silver in a zigzag

explain.ja: 一方、▲4六銀と斜めに銀を進めれば、△4五歩と打たれても元の場所に逃げられます。銀を前に出すときは斜めに動くのがよいです。状況によってはまっすぐのほうがよい場合もありますが、斜めのほうが好手になることが多いです。
explain.en: On the other hand, advancing diagonally with ▲4六銀 lets the silver retreat to its original square even if △4五歩 is dropped. When moving a silver forward, going diagonally is better. Depending on the situation going straight can be better, but diagonal is often the better move.

section.ja: 銀は千鳥に使え!!斜めに動かして使おう
section.en: Use the silver in a zigzag! Move it diagonally

explain.ja: ここから銀を使った3つの手筋を紹介します。図3-1の形は「割打ちの銀」で、銀による両取りです。飛車や金のように斜め後ろに動けない駒を狙います。ただし後手が△5二飛と逃げれば結局銀金交換になるので、駒を取る手筋というより、銀金交換で相手の陣形を乱す手筋です。金は相手の囲いの要の駒なので、囲いの駒を1枚剥がしながら飛車のラインをずらす手筋と考えるとよいです。
explain.en: Here are three tesuji using the silver. The shape in Figure 3-1 is "wari-uchi no gin" (splitting silver), a fork with a silver aimed at pieces that cannot move diagonally backward, like rook and gold. However, if White flees with △5二飛 it becomes just a silver-for-gold exchange, so it is less a way of winning a piece than a way of upsetting the opponent's formation by that exchange. The gold is usually a key piece of the castle, so think of it as stripping one castle piece while knocking the rook off its line.

title.en: Figure 4-1: Silver on the knight's head

explain.ja: 相手の桂馬の頭に銀を打つ手筋を「桂頭の銀」と言います。これで相手の桂馬がどこに逃げても銀で取れる形になります。桂馬が逃げても逃げなくても銀で取れます。
explain.en: Dropping a silver on the head of the opponent's knight is the "keitou no gin" (silver on the knight's head) tesuji. Wherever the knight flees, the silver can capture it; it is taken whether it moves or not.

title.ja: 図5-1 銀1枚でどうやって寄せる？
title.en: Figure 5-1: How to finish with one silver?

explain.ja: 最後は図5-1の局面です。すぐ相手玉を寄せられそうですが、どう指すのがよいでしょうか。
explain.en: Last is the position in Figure 5-1. It looks like the king can be closed in immediately, but how should it be played?

title.ja: 図5-2 銀で王手すると逃げられてしまう
title.en: Figure 5-2: If you check with the silver, the king escapes

explain.ja: ▲3一銀と打って王手したくなりますが、△1三玉と逃げられて失敗します。「王手は追う手」という言葉があり、寄せきれないときに下手な王手をかけると、玉を逃がす手伝いになります。
explain.en: Checking with ▲3一銀 is tempting, but △1三玉 escapes and it fails. As the saying "check is a chasing move" goes, an inept check when you can't finish only helps the king escape.

explain.ja: ここでは直接王手せず、▲2二銀と打つのが正解です。このように相手玉の横に銀を打つ手筋を「腹銀」と言います。この腹銀は、次の▲2三銀成の詰みと、▲3一馬、△1二玉、▲2一銀の詰みを見ており、この2通りの詰みを後手は受けられないので、腹銀を打った局面で必至になります。
explain.en: Here the correct move is not to check directly but to drop ▲2二銀. A silver dropped beside the enemy king like this is called harabgin (腹銀, belly silver). It threatens two mates: ▲2三銀成, and ▲3一馬, △1二玉, ▲2一銀. White cannot defend against both, so the position after the belly silver is brinkmate.

explain.ja: ここでは直接王手せず、▲2二銀と打つのが正解です。このように相手玉の横に銀を打つ手筋を「腹銀」といいます。この腹銀は、次の▲2三銀成の詰みと、▲3一馬 △1二玉 ▲2一銀の詰みを狙っています。後手はこの2通りの詰みを同時に受けられないため、腹銀の局面で必死となります。
explain.en: Here the correct move is not a direct check but dropping the silver with ▲2二銀. This tesuji of dropping a silver beside the enemy king is called a "hara-gin". It threatens two mates: ▲2三銀成, and ▲3一馬 △1二玉 ▲2一銀. White cannot defend against both, so the position after the hara-gin is a forced mate threat (hisshi).

explain.ja: 腹銀を打った局面では、▲3一馬 △1二玉 ▲2一銀という詰みが見えています。▲2三銀成の詰みと合わせて両方を受けることはできません。
explain.en: From the belly-silver position, ▲3一馬 △1二玉 ▲2一銀 is a mate threat. Combined with the ▲2三銀成 mate, White cannot stop both.
